standard_prerequisites: The second-order Peano axioms PA2: the first eight arithmetical axioms plus the second-order induction axiom, and the notion of a model of a second-order theory.
The standardness theorem for PA2 of the same unit: the domain of any model of PA2 is exhausted by the values of the numerals; published as corpus card X2-logic-sol-metatheory-pa2-standard-domain.
The standardness of models of Q proved in the models-of-arithmetic unit: any model of Q whose domain is exhausted by numeral values is isomorphic to the standard natural numbers.
Every model of PA2 is in particular a model of Q, since Q's axioms are among the arithmetical axioms of PA2.
core_obligations: Let M be any model of PA2; by the standardness theorem for PA2, the domain of M is exhausted by the values of the numerals.
Any model of PA2 is also a model of Q; by the standardness of models of Q, any such model whose domain is exhausted by numeral values is standard, that is, isomorphic to the standard natural numbers.
Conclude that any two models of PA2 are each isomorphic to the standard natural numbers, hence isomorphic to each other.
proof_roadmap: Three-step composition: the PA2 standardness theorem exhausts the domain by numerals, membership of Q's axioms in PA2 passes the model down to Q, and the Q standardness theorem upgrades numeral-exhaustion to isomorphism with the standard naturals; uniqueness up to isomorphism follows by composing the two isomorphisms.
difficulty_reason: A composition of two standardness theorems with one observation (Q's axioms are among PA2's); the care point is keeping track of which exhaustion hypothesis each cited theorem consumes and composing the isomorphisms.
